summary: The reviewed initial #5276 analysis distinguishes an accessible census of 12,175 native issue/PR records from a selected runtime cohort of 34 issues and 74 attributed invocations. Observed response envelopes and commit-gap caps are duration proxies, not verified continuous active work; preserve native-completed, unsuccessful, open, reopened and stopped cases, with explicit clock and censoring coverage. Native-completed runtime envelope-to-closure association with baseline hardness was weak; H and the full D1-D8 vector did not improve fixed exploratory parent-group prediction over a training-median baseline. An inverse text-length association lost its pooled advantage under equal-parent weighting or removal of the largest parent component. D8 was constant and D7 nearly constant in the runtime cohort, which was concentrated in November. These are scoped exploratory findings, not population validity or learned routing. Both observed worker model groups used high effort; medium-effort observations belonged to analysts. Different roles/stages, missing frozen task state and disconnected worker profile support do not establish model/effort invariance. First-observed-dispatch body revisions must be distinguished from later accepted bodies; native comment-based review declarations can be absent from native review objects. Three synthetic spelling-task probes changed H from 1 to 19 or 18 when irrelevant exclusions or quoted historical context were appended, demonstrating semantic sensitivity of the unchanged lexical rubric, not prevalence. Literal categorical-policy conformance is distinct from construct validity. Preserve original evidence and all comparisons; report inconclusive support rather than fitting around it. Full #5276 calibration/held-out acceptance remains open. The prior #5249 attribution diagnostic is retained without silent supersession. This record captures source analysis only; it does not establish protected merge, installed adoption, current runtime activity or routing activation.
title: Historical hardness validity requires clock, cohort and profile support
